analysis.overall: You spent 87% of the day in range with a strong 136 mg/dL average, anchored by a very smooth morning despite a couple of stubborn meal spikes.

events.title: Lunch spike and quick drop
events.description: Glucose rose to 203 mg/dL after a 50g carb lunch, but the active insulin caught up fast, sending levels down to 76 mg/dL before self-correcting.

events.title: Steady dinner
events.description: A 40g carb dinner was bolused cleanly, keeping readings flat in the 80–110 mg/dL target zone for several hours.

events.title: Overnight creep
events.description: Levels slowly climbed to 194 mg/dL late at night, taking multiple small corrections before finally coming back down around 4:00 AM.

events.title: Flat morning baseline
events.description: After the overnight corrections settled, glucose locked into a beautifully steady line around 85–90 mg/dL all morning.

events.title: Breakfast peak
events.description: A 30g breakfast spiked glucose up to 231 mg/dL, requiring follow-up correction boluses to bring it back down past noon.

analysis.watch_for_tomorrow: Consider giving breakfast boluses a bit more lead time to help soften the late-morning rise.
